title: Inverse image comparison for free module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], so that $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ is left adjoint to $f_*$ and preserves finite limits. Let $\mathcal B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$; give $f^{-1}\mathcal B$ the ring operations obtained by applying $f^{-1}$ to those of $\mathcal B$ through the finite-product comparisons, and likewise make $f^{-1}$ of a $\mathcal B$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] an $f^{-1}\mathcal B$-module sheaf. For a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ and a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on a site, the free $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $\mathcal O[\mathcal F]$ is the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (in particular a sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]) of the presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $U\mapsto\mathcal O(U)[\mathcal F(U)]$, the free $\mathcal O(U)$-module with basis $\{[s]:s\in\mathcal F(U)\}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with restrictions $\sum a_s[s]\mapsto\sum a_s|_V[s|_V]$; its generator map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal O[\mathcal F]$ (as sheaves of sets) is induced by $s\mapsto[s]$. Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal E$ on $\mathcal C$ there is a canonical isomorphism of $f^{-1}\mathcal B$-module sheaves $f^{-1}(\mathcal B[\mathcal E])\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^{-1}\mathcal B)[f^{-1}\mathcal E]$ which carries $f^{-1}$ of the generator map of $\mathcal B[\mathcal E]$ to the generator map of $(f^{-1}\mathcal B)[f^{-1}\mathcal E]$. It is natural in $\mathcal E$ and in ring-sheaf maps $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B_1$. It is compatible with finite products: for a finite family $(\mathcal E_i)$ and $\mathcal E=\prod_i\mathcal E_i$, its composite with the map of free modules induced by the comparison $\lambda:f^{-1}\prod_i\mathcal E_i\cong\prod_if^{-1}\mathcal E_i$ carries $f^{-1}$ of the generator map to the generator map of $(f^{-1}\mathcal B)[\prod_if^{-1}\mathcal E_i]$ composed with $\lambda$. For the identity geometric morphism it is the identity, and for composable geometric morphisms the comparison of the composite equals the composite of the two comparisons.

source.place: Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials and proof (free-module relation-map comparison under exact inverse image); the free-module comparison is the coproduct/adjunction calculation in the displayed construction.

proof.text: Write $L=f^{-1}$, $R=f_*$ and $B\{E\}$ for the free module sheaf in the statement. Its model is the module sheafification of $P(U)=B(U)[E(U)]$, with restriction $\sum b_e[e]\mapsto\sum(b_e|_V)[e|_V]$. For any $B$-module sheaf $M$ and sheaf map $a:E\to |M|$, the formula $\sum b_e[e]\mapsto\sum b_ea(e)$ defines a unique sectionwise linear map $P\to M$: it commutes with restrictions since $a$ does. The module-sheafification universal property extends it uniquely to $B\{E\}\to M$. Conversely restrict a linear map to the generator map $i:E\to|B\{E\}|$. These operations are inverse, giving $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\{E\},M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E,|M|)$, natural in both arguments. This same construction applies on the target site with the ring $LB$.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof: definition of O_2[F] and linear extension from generators; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: Apply the geometric-module transport theorem with $A=S=LB$, $e_R$ the identity on the transported ring, and $c=\operatorname{id}_{LB}$. Its hypotheses are exactly the small sites, the adjunction $L\dashv R$, and finite-limit preservation of $L$ in the present geometric morphism. The theorem gives the transported module $LM$ with underlying sheaf $L|M|$ and the $B$-module $R_BH$ with underlying sheaf $R|H|$ (scalars act through the unit $B\to RLB$). It gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{LB}(LM,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,R_BH)$ whose underlying map is the original set-sheaf adjunction. Thus this is precisely inverse image with transported scalars; no extension to a different coefficient ring occurs.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules, with the product-transport constructions of Tags 03D1 and 03D2

proof.text: For any $LB$-module sheaf $H$, apply step 2 with $M=B\{E\}$, then step 1, then the set-sheaf adjunction: $\operatorname{Hom}_{LB}(L(B\{E\}),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\{E\},R_BH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E,R|H|)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(LE,|H|)$. The normalization clause of the transport theorem and naturality of the set adjunction show that this composite sends $h$ to $|h|\circ Li$: the adjunct of $h$ composed with $i$ is the adjunct of $h\circ Li$. Hence $L(B\{E\})$, with generator map $Li$, has the free universal property on $LE$.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; the free-module identifications used in Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials

proof.text: Let $j:LE\to |(LB)\{LE\}|$ be the canonical generator map. By step 1 there is a unique linear $q:(LB)\{LE\}\to L(B\{E\})$ with $qj=Li$; by step 3 there is a unique linear $p:L(B\{E\})\to(LB)\{LE\}$ with $p(Li)=j$. The composite $pq$ fixes $j$ and is the identity by step 1. The composite $qp$ fixes $Li$ and is the identity by step 3. Thus $p$ is the required canonical isomorphism. The identity $p(Li)=j$ is the precise generator-preservation assertion, formulated as a map of sheaves and therefore covering all generalized sections, without assuming that a section of an inverse image lifts globally.

source.place: Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials, its three free-module comparisons, justified by the preceding adjunction computation

proof.text: For a sheaf map $u:E\to F$, the two composites from $L(B\{E\})$ to $(LB)\{LF\}$ in the naturality square both restrict on $LE$ to $j_F\circ Lu$; they agree by step 3. The same check with the linear extension of $[e]\mapsto[u(e)]$ proves compatibility with a coefficient-ring map $B\to B_1$, interpreting the maps as semilinear and restricting target scalars to $LB$. For a finite family $E_1,\ldots,E_n$, put $E=\prod E_i$ and let $\lambda:L(\prod E_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod LE_i$ be the finite-product comparison supplied by left exactness. The comparison of step 4 followed by the free-module map induced by $\lambda$ sends its generator to $j\circ\lambda$. This characterizes it uniquely by step 3 and proves compatibility with the product identification. In particular its squares for every product projection commute by the naturality just proved; the empty product is covered by $L1\cong1$.

source.place: Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials, especially the comparison for O_2[O_2 times O_2]; naturality of the free-generator maps

proof.text: For the identity geometric morphism, $p$ fixes the generator map and so is the identity by step 1. For another geometric inverse image $K$, compare $p_{KL}:KL(B\{E\})\to(KLB)\{KLE\}$ with $p_K\circ K(p_L)$, using the composite inverse-image and product comparisons in the definition of composition. Both send the common generator $KLi$ to the generator of $(KLB)\{KLE\}$: for the second map apply $K$ to $p_L(Li)=j_L$ and then use $p_K(Kj_L)=j_{KL}$. Applying step 3 to the composite geometric morphism makes the two linear maps equal. This proves the asserted composition compatibility.

source.place: Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials; coherence follows from generator uniqueness and the composite adjunction
